interface.evidence: Original names clk, d, q; single D flip-flop requires q to expose stored data.

semantics.capture: At every positive edge of clk, q takes d sampled at that edge, using nonblocking assignment.
semantics.hold: q holds between positive edges, including falling edges.
semantics.reset: No reset port or reset behavior specified; none added.
semantics.initialization: No initial value specified; leave register uninitialized. Simulation begins unknown until first capture.
semantics.latency: One flip-flop; captured value visible after the positive-edge NBA update; no additional stages.
semantics.evidence: The module should implement a single D flip-flop. Assume all sequential logic is triggered on the positive edge of the clock.

numeric.arithmetic: None; preserve sampled four-state simulation value.

verification.oracle: Independent expected stored value derived from original D flip-flop semantics.
verification.sampling: Drive d away from positive edges; check after NBA settling; check hold before edges and after falling edges.
cases: d changes with clock low and high
unknown and high-impedance capture and recovery
verification.initial_state: No specified power-up value; no requirement asserted before first edge.
verification.timeout: Bounded simulation watchdog with fatal; PASS only after all comparisons.

specification_ambiguities.issue: Original interface says input q although a single D flip-flop requires an output.
specification_ambiguities.resolution: Interpret q as output, retaining its name and one-bit width, to implement the explicit requested flip-flop functionality.
specification_ambiguities.limitation: Literal all-input interface would provide no observable flip-flop output; direction interpretation is necessary.
